categories.main_business_segments: Curtiss-Wright operates through three reportable segments: Aerospace & Industrial, Defense Electronics, and Naval & Power. Aerospace & Industrial focuses on engineered products for commercial aerospace and general industrial markets. Defense Electronics provides advanced electronics and embedded computing solutions primarily for defense applications. Naval & Power delivers propulsion, auxiliary equipment, and critical systems for naval defense and commercial power & process markets.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company leverages advanced engineering, precision manufacturing, and material modification processes such as machining, assembly, and testing. Key technologies include electronic throttle controls, sensors, actuation systems, embedded computing, avionics, flight test instrumentation, naval propulsion systems, and nuclear reactor components. Production methods emphasize high reliability, ruggedization, and compliance with stringent industry and government standards.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Curtiss-Wright serves a diverse customer base including defense prime contractors, U.S. and foreign government agencies, commercial aerospace OEMs (notably Boeing and Airbus), and companies in the energy, industrial, and process sectors. Major end markets are aerospace defense, ground defense, naval defense, commercial aerospace, nuclear power generation, oil & gas, and general industrial applications.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates globally, with principal manufacturing facilities in the U.S. (Arizona, California, New York, North Carolina, Ohio, Pennsylvania, South Carolina), Canada, Mexico, and the United Kingdom. In 2022, 27% of net sales were to customers outside the U.S., with significant operations and sales in the UK, Europe, and Asia.
categories.supply_chain_position: Curtiss-Wright primarily operates as a midstream and downstream supplier, providing highly engineered components, subsystems, and services that are integrated into larger platforms and systems for OEMs, government agencies, and industrial customers. The company is both a prime contractor and a subcontractor, especially in defense and government markets.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company's strategy, 'Pivot to Growth,' emphasizes organic and inorganic growth, operational excellence, and disciplined capital allocation. Curtiss-Wright invests steadily in R&D to drive innovation in areas such as electrification, digitalization, advanced nuclear technologies, and Modular Open Systems Approach (MOSA) for defense electronics. Strategic priorities include expanding in high-growth defense and clean energy markets, leveraging cross-segment synergies, and maintaining technological leadership.
categories.revenue_model: Curtiss-Wright generates revenue primarily through the sale of engineered products and systems, as well as related services such as maintenance, repair, and overhaul. Revenue is recognized both at point-in-time (product delivery) and over time (long-term contracts), with a significant portion derived from government and commercial contracts, including progress payments and milestone billing.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: The company competes with large, well-resourced industrial and defense firms, as well as specialized technology providers. Key competitive factors include technology, price, product quality, performance, supply reliability, and customer service. Curtiss-Wright holds strong positions in niche, mission-critical applications and is recognized for engineering excellence and long-standing customer relationships.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2022, Curtiss-Wright reported $2.56 billion in net sales, $423 million in operating income, and $294 million in net earnings, with a 2% year-over-year sales increase and 11% growth in operating income. The company maintains a robust backlog ($2.6 billion at year-end), strong cash flow, and a healthy balance sheet, supporting ongoing investments and shareholder returns.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Curtiss-Wright delivers highly engineered, mission-critical products and solutions that enhance safety, efficiency, and reliability in demanding environments. Its differentiation lies in deep technical expertise, precision manufacturing, and the ability to provide cost-effective, niche solutions for high-performance platforms. The company leverages decades of experience and cross-market synergies to offer unique value to defense, aerospace, and industrial customers.
